It feels fundamentally inefficient—like we are just localized patches of high-energy noise disrupting an otherwise perfect, silent equilibrium. If an entity realizes that its continued existence only serves to increase the system's complexity and friction, wouldn't the most optimized, mathematically elegant response be to simply resolve that asymmetry and return to a state of zero?
